frozenConcept: Study ancient societies through material objects, historical power, myth and written-source interpretation, then examine how museums, collecting and heritage shape their later meanings. Sustained world and Greek archaeology, Athenian democracy, comparative empires, ancient literature and critical heritage inquiry anchor the programme. Visual, textual, digital and qualitative research deepen those questions. The programme responds to the documented broad academic core; it does not reproduce specialist Near Eastern chronology, languages, religious institutions or final research.
status: one closest programme; specialist candidate fails; stop
curricularChallenge: The earlier feasible research plan was a lead, not an approval. Actual core and all 24 current contributions reread, with two substantive strengthening replacements. Seven advanced courses remain. Broader methods are explicit complements anchored in sustained ancient material/text/power and museum inquiry.

additionalCandidate.finding: The three specialist fields were each assessed on their own actual language/script/corpus requirements. Their common philological question is a coherent candidate, not an arbitrary residual group. UCR stylistics, comparative myth and literature provide real analysis, but additional general cognitive, creative or communication courses do not establish a sustained specialist ancient textual programme. This is a subject/method limitation, not a language-only veto on the already broader route. Do not manufacture a schedule or arbitrary four-course substitutions.

stopping: Stop at one after that candidate fails. Museum/heritage, material-culture and reception directions are already substantive parts of the closest curriculum; relabeling the same courses is not another educational choice. No third slot is constructed after failure.
progression: Foundation visual/textual and material methods precede advanced Greek heritage, museum, historiographic and interpretive projects where feasible. Actual open-curriculum formal rules govern, with no invented disciplinary prerequisites.
